site_article.headline: SpaceX plans $24 billion gas plant and supercomputing site at Starbase, Texas
site_article.dek: A city hearing notice shows SpaceX seeking a property tax abatement for an on-site power plant that would let it avoid a long wait for grid power.
site_article.summary: SpaceX plans to build a gas-fired power plant and a super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas, with initial phases estimated at about $24 billion, according to a public hearing notice. site_article.seo_description: SpaceX wants a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas, estimated at $24 billion, and is seeking a tax abatement.
site_article.answer_summary: SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas, with about $24 billion estimated for the first phases. A tax abatement hearing is set for December 9, 2026.
site_article.hero_alt: A smiling man in a dark suit photographed at an evening event.

paragraphs.text: SpaceX plans to build a gas-fired power plant and a super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas, according to a public hearing notice reported by Bloomberg News and Reuters on November 9, 2026. The notice estimates the capital investment for the initial phases at roughly $24 billion.

The applicant named in the notice is Space Exploration Technologies Corp., which would build, own and operate the facilities. The work may be done in several phases, and the notice leaves room for later expansions beyond the first estimate. The $24 billion figure is not split between the power plant and the computing site.

The project would sit on about 444 acres east of Brownsville, between Boca Chica Boulevard and the Port of Brownsville, in Cameron County. Brownsville released the tract from its zoning jurisdiction on August 29, and Starbase annexed it on September 21, according to local reporting cited by FourWeekMBA.

SpaceX has applied for a property tax abatement under Chapter 312 of the Texas Tax Code, together with an economic development agreement under Chapter 380 of the Local Government Code. The Starbase City Commission is scheduled to consider both at a public meeting at 7 p.m. on December 9, 2026. The notice does not state the size or length of the abatement, and nothing has been approved.

Reuters reported that generating its own electricity could allow SpaceX to avoid a multi-year wait to connect to the main Texas grid. The notice itself gives no figures for generating capacity or for the size of the computing operation.

Local outlets have cited a separate state air permit application that reportedly lists 35 temporary natural gas turbines with about 748 megawatts of capacity for the first phase. Tech Insider and FourWeekMBA both describe those turbine figures as unconfirmed by the city notice. A SpaceX job posting for a millwright at Starbase mentions installing gas turbines and generators for on-site power, without giving a plant size.

A SpaceX affiliate, Lone Star Mineral Development, has separately filed plans for an 8-mile natural gas pipeline to Starbase called Starpipe, scheduled for service by January 2027. Filings reviewed by Reuters in June said that gas would feed a plant converting it into liquid methane for Starship rockets.

SpaceX acquired xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, earlier in 2026. Last month SpaceX reported a 161 percent jump in third-quarter revenue and a ninefold rise in AI revenue, and it has been renting computing capacity to companies including Google and Anthropic, Reuters reported.

The plan arrives as opposition to data centers grows. According to Reuters, voters rejected data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, and Democrats, some of whom campaigned on pausing new projects, won control of Congress and the Texas governor's office in the midterm elections.

The notice shows how AI builders are trying to solve the power problem by bringing generation inside their own fences. For SpaceX, a company town with its own city commission offers a faster path than most developers have, but the December vote and the state's new political leadership still decide how much of the cost local taxpayers share.
The December 9 commission meeting should reveal the terms of the abatement, and any public filing on generating capacity will show how large the computing site is meant to be.
